llm.summary: This skill stores and recalls long-term memory, journal, and state data in Notion as advertised, but users should treat that data as sensitive external persistence.

dimensions.detail: The Notion token and explicit database/data-source IDs are proportionate for this integration, and local reads are mostly limited to workspace memory/dream files for ambient recall when configured.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No hidden package install scripts or dependency execution were found; installation requires Node, a Notion API key, and the notion-api-automation skill, while database setup happens only when the setup script is run.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill includes guardrails for high-signal writes, local-only behavior on request, avoiding secrets and intimate private profile facts, and limiting delegation to read-only analysis; proactive USER.md promotion is disclosed but should be used carefully.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill deliberately persists memory, mood/state, worklog, journal, and profile-relevant facts to Notion and local workspace files; this is expected for the purpose but carries privacy and retention risk.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The Notion database creation, schema patching, memory writes, search, state snapshots, journal entries, ambient recall, and identity/profile helpers match the stated continuity, durable memory, state, journal, and identity-maintenance purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want a Notion-backed long-term memory/journal system. Use a narrowly scoped Notion integration, avoid storing secrets or regulated personal data, review any cron setup and USER.md profile promotion behavior, and do not set NOTIONCTL_PATH or --write paths to locations you do not trust.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The broader Notion database creation, relation/schema management, query, and write capabilities are disclosed in SKILL.md and README.md and are necessary for the advertised Notion-backed memory system.
[SDI-1] expected: Writing memory and journal records to Notion is central to the skill's purpose and is clearly described as externalizing continuity to Notion, though users should understand it may contain sensitive personal or work context.
[SDI-1] expected: The Notion bridge exposes reusable CRUD helpers, but inspected scripts use them for the skill's configured memory, state, journal, and setup flows rather than hidden unrelated access.
[SDI-2] expected: NOTIONCTL_PATH is an optional compatibility override for locating the dependent notionctl script; it is a local environment-controlled execution path and should not be set to untrusted files.
[SQP-2] expected: The README and SKILL.md disclose Notion-backed durable memory, emotional state, and journaling, but the privacy warning is not especially prominent for highly sensitive data.
[SQP-2] expected: Proactive USER.md updates are purpose-aligned and constrained to durable, reusable, safe facts, with explicit exclusions for secrets, financial data, intimate personal data, and raw private facts.
[SQP-2] expected: The local --write/--append helpers and stdout outputs expose or persist recalled state and conflict data when invoked; this is expected for command-line helper tools but users should control paths and logs.
[SQP-2] expected: Ambient recall reads selected workspace memory, dream, conflict, and Notion sources and stages a short local recall with TTL and daily cap; this is documented and bounded, not hidden background exfiltration.
